If he had known that the only way to make the Woman laugh was by having shaky hands, Zhang Aman would have rather stayed uncured.
At least then she would still smile.
But day by day, her brows furrowed deeper, as if nothing could bring her joy anymore.
Even when Zhang Aman carefully handed her flowers or placed sugar cakes on the table, all he received was a sigh.
Frustrated, Zhang Aman lost sleep, desperately seeking what might please her. He even asked a wandering swordsman to stop her and inquire directly.
The Woman sighed, but the swordsman pressed on.
"Then bring me nine thousand nine hundred and ninety-nine moonbeams," she said with a faint smile. The swordsman dismissed it as a jest.
But Zhang Aman took it seriously. Night after night, he gathered moonbeams, even enlisting Passersby to help.
Whether it was gratitude or love, Zhang Aman could no longer tell.
At least his hands no longer trembled. As long as they remained steady, he would keep gathering moonbeams.
Until he saw her smile again.
